title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous and next pages). V is a real Euclidean plane. D is a finite dihedral group of isometries of V containing the central element a_0 = -1. It permutes the vertices R̃_i (i ∈ J̃) of a regular polygon on the unit circle.

One passes to the complexification V_C and the complex projective line Σ = P(V_C). This line contains the real circle Σ_R = P(V). Since a_0 = -1 acts trivially on Σ, the action of D factors through D' = D/{±1}, which is again dihedral. The images R_i ∈ Σ are indexed by J = J̃/{±1}.

This page:
1. Σ_R ≅ S^1 cuts the sphere Σ into two open discs (hemispheres). (14) identifies their set π_0(Σ∖Σ_R) with the two-element set ω = Ω(Σ_R) of orientations of Σ_R. The rule is: each hemisphere, carrying the complex orientation of Σ, induces a boundary orientation on Σ_R by the Stokes convention. Since dim V = 2, orientations of P(V) correspond canonically to orientations of V, so ω is also the set of orientations of V.
2. The fixed points of the rotation part act on Σ as two 'poles', one in each hemisphere. They are therefore indexed by orientations: P_ω = Σ^{D^+} ∩ Σ_ω (15).
3. In linear-algebra terms these are the eigenlines of D^+ in V_C. The text then brings in the Euclidean structure of V, extended to a complex symmetric bilinear form on V_C. The next page continues: V_C = ⊕_ω V_C^ω, a splitting into the two isotropic lines, which are also the eigenlines of all of O^+(V). An orientation ω gives the quarter-turn u_ω with u_ω² = -1, hence a complex structure V_(ω) on V. The universal property of complexification then identifies V_C^ω with an eigenline of u_ω.

So the poles are the classical circular points (isotropic directions) of the Euclidean plane, labelled canonically by the two orientations.

Purpose. The configuration (P^1; the n points R_i on the real circle; the two poles) is the most symmetric genus-0 marked configuration: the n-th roots of unity together with 0 and ∞. Its automorphism group is dihedral. Grothendieck is setting up canonical, coordinate-free labels for the special points (dihedral/'cyclic' base points) used in the genus-0 Teichmüller groupoid. That is why he insists on indexing everything by intrinsic sets (J, ω) rather than by choices.
errors: The opening sentence says the fixed-point set of D' on Σ consists of two points. This is wrong for D' itself. Reflections in D extend to Möbius maps of determinant < 0, which swap the two hemispheres and the two isotropic points, so D' has no fixed points on Σ. The correct statement, which the author uses in (15), concerns the rotation subgroup D^+ (equivalently D'^+).

Implicit hypothesis: D^+/{±1} must be nontrivial, i.e. the polygon has at least 3 classes, so that rotations other than ±1 exist. Otherwise every point of Σ is fixed by D'^+, and the two-pole statement fails. Small cases are not addressed.

ideas.what: Components of P^1(C) minus P^1(R) are canonically indexed by orientations of the real circle (or of V), via the boundary-orientation (Stokes) convention
ideas.modern_name: upper/lower half-plane ↔ orientation of RP^1; boundary orientation convention

ideas.what: Fixed points of the rotation group on P(V_C) are the two isotropic lines (circular points), labelled by orientations; each is an eigenline of the quarter-turn defining a complex structure
ideas.modern_name: circular points at infinity / isotropic lines; Laguerre

ideas.what: Canonical, choice-free description of the dihedrally symmetric marked P^1 (n points on the real circle plus two poles) as special points for the genus-0 Teichmüller groupoid
ideas.modern_name: dihedral / cyclic special points of M_{0,n}, tangential base points with dihedral symmetry
ideas.usually_credited_to: Esquisse d'un programme (Grothendieck 1984); later Ihara, Drinfeld, Lochak–Schneps, Brown (dihedral coordinates)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses dihedral symmetries of M_{0,n} and special points in general terms

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful, canonical rewriting of classical facts: the hemispheres of P^1(C) are indexed by orientations, and the poles are the circular points. It is in Grothendieck's characteristic choice-free style, but contains nothing new or unrecorded.
transcription_corrections: '(cf.[?] couvr. de Stokes' should read '(conv. de Stokes' = convention de Stokes.

'la double structure ensdiédrale[?] sur V_C' is most likely 'la donnée [de la] structure euclidienne sur V(_C)', i.e. the Euclidean structure on V extending to a complex bilinear structure on V_C. This is consistent with the 'sous-espaces isotropes' on the next page.
'donc les deux "pôles" seront indexés par ω, et notés P_ω': the image reads 'et notés P_ω' directly.
